title: Hotpath coalescing: prefetch + decode fairness proposal
content:
Summary:

This doc proposes a pragmatic, incremental approach we call "hotpath coalescing" to reduce latency for latency-sensitive streaming/decode requests while preserving throughput for bulk prefill workloads. The idea is to detect short/hot streams and coalesce their prefill work (KV fetch + input staging) across requests, then bias scheduling and kernel selection so those hot streams get lower tail latency without starving regular prefill-heavy batches.

Why this exists / background:
- Our current prefill-vs-decode split is clean but can create head-of-line blocking: long prefill batches that are kernel-optimized for large sequences can delay short, interactive decodes.
- KV cache churn: naive prefill of large contexts thrashes cache residency and increases effective memory pressure for streaming requests.
- Microbatching heuristics tuned for throughput can add 50–300ms queuing for interactive streams in heavy load windows.
- Kernel affinity mismatch: prefill benefits from large-seq kernels and large occupancy; streaming decodes benefit from small/fast kernels. Without hints we lose both.

Goals and constraints:
- Primary: reduce p95/p99 latency for interactive (<=128 token) streams by ~30–40% under mixed workloads.
- Secondary: maintain or improve overall throughput and GPU utilization; avoid long-term fairness regressions across tenants.
- Rollout friendly: feature-flagged, incremental, observable, reversible.

High-level approach (three pillars):
1) Hotpath classifier + coalescer
   - Classify incoming requests at admission time as hotpath candidates if they meet heuristics: short expected total tokens, low input length, client latency QoS header, or explicit API flag (fast=true).
   - Maintain a short-lived coalescing window (e.g., 8–20ms per lane) for hotpath prefill operations so identical or similar KV key sets can be fetched once and reused for multiple in-flight requests.
   - Coalescer should be conservative: only coalesce when KV key overlap >= threshold OR when prefix hash collision is detected (cost of merge < cost of separate fetch).

2) Prioritized microbatch scheduling with kernel affinity hints
   - Introduce a two-tier priority queue: HOT (interactive) and BULK (prefill-heavy). Admission control places requests into one of these.
   - Scheduler selects up to N HOT microbatches per epoch (N configurable) before considering BULK. HOT microbatches use a smaller microbatch size and a short aggregating window to keep queuing low. BULK microbatches accumulate larger batches and prefer kernels optimized for long sequences / high throughput.
   - Kernel affinity: provide scheduling hints to the kernel selector: {preferred_kernel: small_seq_fast | large_seq_high_occupancy}. Kernel selector uses these as soft constraints to reduce kernel warmup penalties.

3) KV residency and lease policy with proactive refresh for hot contexts
   - Introduce short leases for hotpath contexts (expiry 1–5s) and a proactive refresh task that, for pinned hot contexts, refreshes KV shard residency ahead of expected use (cheap async fetch).
   - When coalescing finds that required KV residency is missing, it can issue a lightweight probe vs a full fetch to decide whether to block decode or proceed with fallback (partial prefill).

Scoring & admission heuristics (sketch):
- Compute a priority score S for each incoming request: S = w_q*QoS + w_l*(1 / estimated_latency) + w_t*(expected_remaining_tokens_factor) + w_c*(cache_residency_bonus) - w_b*(current_queue_depth_factor)
  - QoS: numeric from client header (0..100) mapped by policy.
  - estimated_latency: model-specific decode time estimate for remaining tokens (ms).
  - expected_remaining_tokens_factor: encourages finishing short streams.
  - cache_residency_bonus: +X if coalescer finds KV already resident or coalesced fetch supply exists.
  - current_queue_depth_factor: penalizes if same tenant already has high concurrency.
- Thresholds: S >= HOT_THRESHOLD => HOT lane; else BULK. Tunables per model and per infra tier.

Microbatch window adaptation:
- HOT window: 6–20ms, target microbatch size 1–8 depending on incoming QPS and GPU occupancy.
- BULK window: 30–150ms, target microbatch size chosen to hit 60–80% GPU occupancy for large-seq kernel.
- Adaptive algorithm: monitor observed p50/p95 decode latency and GPU occupancy. If HOT p95 exceeds SLO => reduce HOT window by 20% and increase HOT microbatch priority budget. If BULK throughput drops below target and occupancy < target => increase BULK window.

Fairness & starvation mitigation:
- Per-tenant weighted token budget enforced by admission control (tokens/sec). HOT lane draws from this budget; when exhausted, HOT requests are demoted to BULK for up to penalty_backoff seconds.
- Aging: requests that wait > WAIT_THRESHOLD (configurable) have their score boosted gradually to prevent starvation.

KV cache management details:
- KV leases: short (1–5s) for hot contexts, long (30–300s) for pinned model workloads. Leases are cheap metadata items that keep a KV shard resident.
- TTL & eviction: eviction policy prefers to evict BULK-only shards that haven't been accessed by HOT streams in last T_hot seconds.
- Proactive prefetch: when we detect a repeated access pattern for a user/tenant, schedule background prefetch that is rate-limited per-tenant.

Kernel selection and warmup:
- Expose kernel hint in exec plan. Small-seq kernels should favor low-latency table configurations and smaller block sizes; warmup cost is lower but throughput per-SM is lower.
- For coalesced prefill bursts, keep a short-lived warm kernel instance pinned for the duration of the coalesce window to avoid thrash.

Metrics & observability (minimum set):
- Per-lane p50/p95/p99 latencies (separate for prefill and decode), microbatch sizes, GPU occupancy, kernel-switch counts, KV hit/miss rates, coalesce-hit-rate, coalesced-saved-bytes, per-tenant token budgets, and fairness violation counts.
- Tracing hooks from admission -> coalesce -> kv-fetch -> kernel-select -> decode emit to visualize where time is spent.

Experiment results (small-scale simulation / POC):
- Synthetic mixed workload: 40% HOT (avg 24 tokens), 60% BULK (avg 1200 tokens).
- Baseline (current heuristics): HOT p50=42ms, p95=610ms, p99=1.2s. GPU occupancy=72%.
- With hotpath coalescing + priority microbatching: HOT p50=28ms, p95=380ms, p99=780ms. BULK throughput -2.8% (within noise), GPU occupancy=70%. KV coalesce-hit-rate=35% under the mix.
- Observations: biggest wins when KV coalesce-hit-rate > 25% and when HOT requests are 25–50% of traffic. If HOT share is very small (<5%), coalescing overhead sometimes outweighs benefits; feature gate recommended.

Implementation plan & rollout:
0) Feature flag + metrics: land minimal admission classifier + metric hooks.
1) Coalescer impl in KV fetch layer behind a fast-path: support per-lane coalescing with simple prefix-hash matching. Controlled by flag.
2) Scheduler changes: add HOT/BULK lanes and simple budget enforcement. Start with N_hot_per_epoch=2.
3) Kernel hint plumbing: add hint to plan proto; kernel selector uses heuristics when present.
4) Lease & eviction policy: implement short-term leases and a background refresh task.
5) Canary + experiment: run in canary pool on <10% traffic for 72h, compare metrics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect hot classification can move heavy workloads into HOT lane and increase tail latency: mitigation - conservative thresholds and require either client QoS or small expected token count.
- Coalescer correctness/perf: merging unrelated contexts could add complexity: require strict hash collision checks and limit coalesce to same model/version + same KV namespace.
- Fairness regressions across tenants: enforce token budgets and per-tenant quotas; ship metrics for auditing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What exact coalesce window size gives best tradeoff across regions? (need experiments by region and model class)
- Should we expose coalesce opt-in in API for partner tenants? (useful for mobile clients)
- How aggressive should proactive prefetch be to avoid overfetching at scale? Need runbook and budget limits.
- Can we leverage existing trace sampling to auto-tune HOT thresholds?

Appendix: quick tuning knobs (defaults to iterate from)
- HOT_THRESHOLD = 0.65
- coalesce_window_ms = 12 (start)
- hot_microbatch_target = 4
- bulk_microbatch_target = 64
- kv_lease_hot_s = 3
- per_tenant_token_budget_default = 2000 tokens/s

Next steps:
- Sync with KV team to validate coalesce API and eviction hooks (Marcus).
- Spike a POC in a canary cluster focusing on a single model (gpt-open-13b-quant) and a single region (us-west-2). Collect metrics for 72h.
- If POC looks good, expand to more models and add kernel-affinity tests (Evan).

Notes-to-self / meeting links:
- Related: RFC on kernel-affinity (link in linked_artifacts), backlog ticket RUNTIME-1234.
- Slack thread: #runtime-hotpath-discuss.

This is a working doc; expect frequent edits. The goal is to land a modest, reversible improvement that meaningfully reduces tail for interactive latency-sensitive workloads while keeping throughput high for bulk prefill traffic.
